name: a-global-option-in-front-of-a-read-only-git-command-is-allowed
description: BL2/T318 retry. The other precision half: after `-C` and its value are skipped, `status` is what the subcommand test sees, and `status` is none of the four restore verbs - so this rule never asks it anything, exactly as fixture 101 pins for the bare read-only shapes. Together with 105 this proves the fix skips the option's VALUE and not the SUBCOMMAND: a walker that ate one token too many would land on `.keel/audit/keel-audit.jsonl` here and on nothing at all in `git -C /tmp status`, and the fail-closed look-ahead would then be reachable by any read. Like 105 it passes against the pre-fix code too; it guards the direction that code was accidentally right about.
